front_blocks.md: What is meant by the term **price elasticity of supply (PES)**?

back_blocks.md: Price elasticity of supply reveals how responsive the **change in quantity supplied** is to a change in price.

cards.front_md: What is meant by the term **price elasticity of supply (PES)**?
cards.back_md: Price elasticity of supply reveals how responsive the **change in quantity supplied** is to a change in price.

front_blocks.md: State the **price elasticity of supply (PES) formula**.

back_blocks.md: PES = % change in QS ÷ % change in P

cards.front_md: State the **price elasticity of supply (PES) formula**.
cards.back_md:
**Formula:**

PES = % change in QS ÷ % change in P

back_blocks.md: Price inelastic supply occurs when the percentage change in quantity supplied is **less than proportional **to the percentage change in price.

cards.back_md: Price inelastic supply occurs when the percentage change in quantity supplied is **less than proportional **to the percentage change in price.

front_blocks.md: What does **unitary elasticity of supply** mean?

back_blocks.md: Unitary elasticity of supply means the percentage change in quantity supplied is **exactly equal **to the percentage change in price.

cards.front_md: What does **unitary elasticity of supply** mean?
cards.back_md: Unitary elasticity of supply means the percentage change in quantity supplied is **exactly equal **to the percentage change in price.

back_blocks.md: Price elastic supply is when the percentage change in quantity supplied is **more than proportional **to the percentage change in price.

cards.back_md: Price elastic supply is when the percentage change in quantity supplied is **more than proportional **to the percentage change in price.

front_blocks.md: State the meaning of perfectly **price inelastic supply**.

back_blocks.md: Perfectly price inelastic supply occurs when the quantity supplied is **completely unresponsive** to a change in price.

cards.front_md: State the meaning of perfectly **price inelastic supply**.
cards.back_md: Perfectly price inelastic supply occurs when the quantity supplied is **completely unresponsive** to a change in price.

front_blocks.md: What impact do **mobile factors of production** have on PES?

back_blocks.md: If producers can quickly **switch resources between products** (mobile factors of production), then supply will be more price elastic.

cards.front_md: What impact do **mobile factors of production** have on PES?
cards.back_md: If producers can quickly **switch resources between products** (mobile factors of production), then supply will be more price elastic.

front_blocks.md: What impact does **spare capacity** have on PES?

back_blocks.md: If there is **spare capacity **to increase production when prices rise, then supply will be **price elastic**. If there is no spare capacity, supply will be price inelastic.

cards.front_md: What impact does **spare capacity** have on PES?
cards.back_md: If there is **spare capacity **to increase production when prices rise, then supply will be **price elastic**. If there is no spare capacity, supply will be price inelastic.

front_blocks.md: State the formula for calculating a **percentage change**.

back_blocks.md: % Change = (New Value - Old Value) ÷ Old Value x 100

cards.front_md: State the formula for calculating a **percentage change**.
cards.back_md:
**Formula:**

% Change = (New Value - Old Value) ÷ Old Value x 100

front_blocks.md: Short term supply is often **more price elastic** for agricultural products.

back_blocks.md: In the short run it is harder for producers to respond to price increases, as it takes time to grow crops, so supply is more price inelastic.

cards.front_md:
**True or False? **

Short term supply is often **more price elastic** for agricultural products.
cards.back_md:
**False. **

In the short run it is harder for producers to respond to price increases, as it takes time to grow crops, so supply is more price inelastic.

front_blocks.md: What is the impact of the **ability to store goods** on PES?

back_blocks.md: If products can be easily stored, then **PES will be higher (more elastic)** as producers can quickly increase supply.

cards.front_md: What is the impact of the **ability to store goods** on PES?
cards.back_md: If products can be easily stored, then **PES will be higher (more elastic)** as producers can quickly increase supply.
